plan.description: Execute the actual Raft.pipelineDecode with one instrumented AppendFuture and observe whether Error returned before Response was invoked. Stop at that invocation without supplying response fields.

scope.description: One delivered AppendFuture consumed by Raft.pipelineDecode. Check the ordering and result of Error() relative to Response() and response-field interpretation.
assumptions: The pipeline supplies an AppendFuture governed by the attached AppendFuture interface contract.
The consumer receives the future before its stop branch terminates processing.
excluded: Establishing a network history that produces an errored future with success-looking response fields
Proving incorrect follower progress, commitment, leadership behavior, or application effects
General pipeline shutdown and cancellation guarantees

harness.description: A buffered Consumer channel supplies exactly one future while the stop channel remains open. The actual consumer executes synchronously. Request records receipt; Response records the Error-return state, prior Request invocation, stop-channel readiness, and fixture completion status, then raises a uniquely typed sentinel recovered by the test. These interfaces control delivery and the observation endpoint without network scheduling assumptions. Test assertions establish endpoint reachability; the correlated event checker evaluates the interface requirement.
semantic_changes: Replace the transport-facing AppendPipeline and AppendFuture with instrumented interface implementations for this consumer contract experiment.
Use an already completed successful future whose Error returns its stored nil completion error; observe whether the consumer actually calls it.
Terminate execution at Response entry with a recovered sentinel instead of returning response fields. This observation adaptation prevents all subsequent field interpretation and downstream effects.

Construct zero-valued Raft and followerReplication objects because the supplied consumer source accesses no initialized Raft services before this endpoint and uses only the follower peer lock and peer value.
Record observable legality fields at Response entry without changing the actual consumer or its invocation order.

legality.derivation: pipelineDecode accepts AppendPipeline directly. Its acquired body receives a future, reads the peer under its lock, and calls Request followed by Response before accessing metrics or response fields. The experiment supplies a completed future with a stable nil error, a valid request pointer, and an open stop channel. The result event records whether Request actually ran, whether the stop channel remains unready, and whether the stored completion error is nil. These legality conditions do not assume that Error was called. The explicit AppendFuture contract independently requires Error to return before Response. The recovered sentinel is an observation boundary, not a transport error or evidence of a target panic.
legality.applicability: Consumer-side method ordering for one interface-delivered, successfully completed future. The interface substitution supports this local endpoint only.
unresolved: The experiment does not instantiate the concrete network appendFuture.
The sentinel prevents evaluating response-field validity and downstream consequences.
alternatives: Producer-side completion can precede delivery, but the explicit interface still requires Error to return before Response invocation.

grounding.derivation: AppendFuture.Response explicitly requires Error to have returned. The observed boolean is updated only by the instrumented Error method as it returns, and sampled at Response entry. Execution is synchronous, so Response cannot observe that update until Error has returned to its caller. The actual pipelineDecode call determines invocation order. The prerequisite carries the interface-required value; it is normative input, not a fabricated implementation observation.
grounding.applicability: The first Response invocation on the independently identified future received by the actual consumer.
unresolved: Successful completion is supplied by the interface fixture; concrete network failure reachability is outside this comparison.
This checker covers the ordering conjunct of the obligation, not the separate restriction on interpreting fields after a non-nil Error.
alternatives: Completion synchronization before delivery could make fields visible without satisfying the explicit method-call precondition.

observable_properties.description: For the same delivered future, Error must have returned before Response is invoked. Compare the state observed at Response entry with the interface requirement recorded at the preceding Request invocation.

uncertainties: The instrumented interface experiment establishes only actual consumer invocation ordering; it does not reproduce NetworkTransport behavior.
The non-nil Error response-validity branch remains unchecked because execution stops at Response entry.
Concrete appendFuture synchronization remains unread and no conclusion about its memory visibility is drawn.
No follower progress, commitment, leadership, contact, or application consequence is observed.
A passing Go test indicates the observation endpoint was reached; only the correlated event comparison determines this property's outcome.
